sections.h2: Who sets and collects property tax in New Hanover County?
sections.html:
The New Hanover County Tax Department values property and sends the bills, and the elected county and municipal boards set the rates. The county's revaluation page describes tax as two parts: the assessed value of the property and a rate per $100 of value.

The Tax Department number is (910) 798-7300. The county says these taxes are its largest revenue source, funding public education, emergency medical services, public health, law enforcement, affordable housing and other programs. The county covers 192.26 square miles of land and counted 245,959 residents on July 1, 2025, a 9.0% rise over the April 2020 base.

sections.h2: What are the 2026-27 property tax rates in New Hanover County?
sections.html:
The county rate is 30.6 cents per $100 of value for fiscal year 2026-2027. Owners in the unincorporated county pay an added fire services rate of 7.25 cents per $100, and city or town rates apply on top for owners inside a municipality.

sections.h2: When are New Hanover County property tax bills due?
sections.html:
Bills are mailed in the summer and are due September 1. The county says they can be paid without interest through January 5, which tracks G.S. 105-360, where par payment runs until January 6 and interest starts on or after that date.

Once interest begins, the statute charges 2% from January 6 until February 1, and then three-fourths of one percent for each month or fraction after that. A county or city may also adopt a prepayment discount schedule, and mailed payments count as received on the USPS postmark date.

The county includes four payment coupons with each bill so an owner can pay in four equal installments. Payment options listed in the county's release include:

  • Credit card, debit card and e-check payments at the Tax Office, with a service fee when paying online.
  • Online payment through InvoiceCloud, or by phone at 1-877-309-0878.
  • An outdoor drop box beside the main entrance of the Government Center.
  • Mail to New Hanover County Tax, PO Box 18000, Wilmington, NC 28406.

Owners who pay through escrow receive a courtesy notice and should confirm with the mortgage company that the bill was paid. Owners who fall behind are asked to call before January 6 to set up a payment plan.

sections.h2: How often does New Hanover County reappraise real estate?
sections.html:
Every four years. State law requires a reappraisal at least every eighth year (G.S. 105-286), but the county commissioners shortened the cycle to four years in 2008 because of fast growth. The latest revaluation took effect January 1, 2025, and the one before it took effect January 1, 2021.

The county sorts roughly 115,000 parcels into about 1,500 neighborhoods of similar market, economic and geographic conditions, reviews sales of homes and land, and builds a Schedule of Values that the Board of Commissioners must approve. In between, real property is permanently listed, so owners do not file a yearly listing for it. They must still list new improvements during the regular January listing period, and the Tax Department will list them for an owner who asks for help.

Value can also change outside a revaluation year for the reasons in G.S. 105-287, and the county says it sends written notice any time it changes a value.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a New Hanover County assessment?
sections.html:
Start by calling the Tax Department or filing an appeal form, then move to the Board of Equalization and Review if the informal review does not settle it. Under the county's rules, an owner may appeal in any year between January 1 and the board's adjournment.

The county encourages appeals within 30 days of the value notice, but the hard deadline is the board's adjournment date. For the 2026 tax year that date was May 14, 2026, at 5:00 pm, and it has passed. Each year the Board of Equalization and Review meets between the first Monday in April and the first Monday in May, and the county mails its written decision within 30 days of the meeting.

Know who may speak for the owner before filing:

  • Individual owners may represent themselves, and any one joint owner may act for the others.
  • North Carolina attorneys may file and appear without a signed power of attorney.
  • Business entities may use an officer, a manager, a W-2 employee or an owner with at least 25% interest, with written authority.
  • Other non-attorney representatives are allowed only for good cause, such as illness, a death in the family or active-duty deployment.

If the board's answer still does not satisfy you, G.S. 105-290 gives 30 days from the date the board mailed its decision to file a written notice of appeal with the Property Tax Commission, with a copy to the county assessor.

sections.h2: What tax relief can a New Hanover County homeowner claim?
sections.html:
North Carolina offers three relief programs, and an owner may receive only one of them. All are filed on Form AV-9 with the county assessor, not with the Department of Revenue.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion (G.S. 105-277.1): the greater of $25,000 or 50% of appraised value, for owners 65 or older, or totally and permanently disabled, within the income limit. The 2026 income limit is $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion (G.S. 105-277.1C): the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income limit.
  • Circuit breaker (G.S. 105-277.1B): tax capped at 4.0% of income, or 5.0% when income is above the limit and up to 150% of it, which the form prints as $58,200 for 2026.

The form should be filed during the January listing period, but the assessor must accept it through June 1 before the tax year. The circuit breaker needs a new application every year, and under it the unpaid excess is deferred and carries a lien. If the owner sells, the deferred taxes for the previous three fiscal years come due.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid New Hanover County taxes when a house is sold?
sections.html:
They follow the parcel. G.S. 105-355 attaches the lien on the date property is listed under G.S. 105-285, and it brings penalties, interest and costs with it, so the debt stays with the parcel through a sale.

That is why a payoff figure matters before closing. Ask the Tax Department at (910) 798-7300 for the amount due on the parcel and give it to the closing attorney. If the taxes stay unpaid, the county can bring a foreclosure action under G.S. 105-374 in the county where the property sits. Sale is at public auction at the courthouse door, a commissioner may require a deposit of up to 20% of the bid, and an upset bid or exceptions may be filed within 10 days of the report of sale. Before confirmation, a person can redeem by paying all taxes, penalties, interest and costs.

sections.h2: What do New Hanover County property values look like?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau puts the median value of an owner-occupied home at $387,800 for 2020 to 2024, with median owner costs of $1,888 a month for homes with a mortgage and $658 without one. Median household income was $75,166 and 21.3% of residents were 65 or older, a group that may qualify for the exclusions above.

With 2,332 building permits issued in 2025 and a density of 1,174.0 people per square mile, a seller with a house that needs work should check whether any improvements were listed with the Tax Department, since new construction and additions are valued through the January listing process.

faqs.q: When are New Hanover County property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due September 1 and can be paid without interest until January 5, according to the county. Statute then adds 2% for January 6 to February 1, and three-fourths of one percent for each month after.

faqs.q: What is the New Hanover County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The county rate is 30.6 cents per $100 for fiscal year 2026-2027, plus 7.25 cents per $100 for fire services in the unincorporated county. City of Wilmington owners add 33.15 cents per $100.

faqs.q: How often does New Hanover County revalue property?
faqs.a: Every four years. The most recent revaluation took effect January 1, 2025, and the cycle before that took effect January 1, 2021.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal my New Hanover County value?
faqs.a: Only through the Board of Equalization and Review adjournment date for the tax year, and the 2026 deadline of May 14, 2026 has passed. Call (910) 798-7300 to ask about the next reappraisal window or a value change notice.

faqs.q: Do I have to pay back taxes when I sell a house in New Hanover County?
faqs.a: Yes, unpaid taxes are a lien on the parcel, so they must be cleared at or before closing. Ask the Tax Department for a payoff amount and give it to the closing attorney.
